What Is a Prop Firm? A Plain-English Guide

A proprietary trading firm, or prop firm, gives traders access to a funded account in exchange for passing an evaluation. The trader keeps a share of the profits and the firm keeps the rest.

How prop firms make money

Most modern prop firms earn revenue from evaluation fees and from the spread between trader payouts and simulated account performance. Understanding the evaluation is the first step for any new trader.

Evaluations and challenges

An evaluation sets a profit target, a maximum daily loss and a maximum overall drawdown. Traders who pass the challenge are offered a funded account with a profit split.

Profit splits

Profit splits usually start around 80 percent for the trader and can scale higher with consistent performance. The exact split depends on the firm and the account size you choose.

Risks for traders

The main risk for traders is paying repeated evaluation fees without passing. Nothing about a funded account guarantees a payout, and a disciplined risk plan matters more than the account size.
